title: Ghormeh Sabzi
instructions: Finely chop the parsley, cilantro, chives, and fenugreek leaves.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a large pan and fry the chopped herbs over medium heat for 20 minutes until darkened and fragrant, then set aside.
In a large pot, heat the remaining oil and sauté the diced onion until golden.
Add the lamb stew meat and turmeric, and brown the meat on all sides.
Pour in the water, add the fried herbs, and bring to a boil.
Prick the dried limes with a fork, add them to the pot, and season with salt and black pepper.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Add the cooked red kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes until the oil separates and the stew thickens.
Taste and adjust seasoning before serving hot with steamed rice.

title: Fesenjan
instructions: Grind the walnuts finely in a food processor until they form a coarse paste.
Heat the oil in a pot and sauté the diced onion until soft and translucent.
Add the chicken thighs and turmeric, and sear until lightly browned on both sides.
Stir in the ground walnuts and 500 ml of the water, then bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover and cook over low heat for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Add the pomegranate paste, sugar, salt, and black pepper, along with the remaining water.
Continue simmering uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce turns thick and deep brown.
Taste and balance the sweet-tart flavor by adjusting sugar or pomegranate paste as needed.
Serve hot over steamed white rice.

title: Zereshk Polo
instructions: Rinse the basmati rice several times until the water runs clear, then soak in salted water for 1 hour.
Bloom the saffron in 3 tablespoons of hot water and set aside.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add salt, then add the drained rice and boil for 6 to 8 minutes until slightly softened.
Drain the rice and rinse gently with lukewarm water.
Layer the parboiled rice back into the pot, drizzle with 2 tablespoons of melted butter, cover, and steam on low heat for 40 minutes.
Meanwhile, rinse the barberries and pick out any stems or debris.
In a small pan, melt the remaining butter and lightly sauté the barberries with sugar for 2 to 3 minutes, being careful not to burn them.
Spoon a portion of the steamed rice into a bowl and mix with the bloomed saffron water.
Serve the plain rice on a platter, top with the saffron rice and sautéed barberries just before serving.

title: Tahchin
instructions: Rinse the basmati rice until the water runs clear and soak in salted water for 1 hour.
Bloom the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water.
Boil the chicken breast with the sliced onion, salt, and black pepper until fully cooked, then shred the meat and reserve the broth.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and parboil the drained rice for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain.
In a bowl, whisk the egg yolks, yogurt, half of the bloomed saffron water, and a ladle of the reserved chicken broth.
Fold half of the parboiled rice into the yogurt mixture until well combined.
Oil the bottom of a pot generously and spread half of the yogurt-rice mixture evenly across the base.
Layer the shredded chicken over the rice, then top with the remaining plain parboiled rice.
Cover with a lid wrapped in a clean towel and cook on low heat for 45 to 60 minutes until a golden crust forms on the bottom.
Invert the pot onto a large serving plate to reveal the crispy golden layer and serve hot.

title: Joojeh Kabab
instructions: Cut the chicken thighs into large cubes and place them in a mixing bowl.
Grate the onions and add them to the bowl along with the lemon juice, oil, salt, and black pepper.
Bloom the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water and pour it over the chicken.
Mix everything thoroughly, cover, and marinate in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Thread the marinated chicken pieces onto skewers.
Preheat a grill or grill pan to medium-high heat.
Grill the skewers for 15 to 20 minutes, turning frequently, until the chicken is cooked through and lightly charred.
Baste with any remaining marinade during grilling for extra flavor.
Serve hot with grilled tomatoes and steamed rice.

title: Kashk-e Bademjan
instructions: Peel the eggplants and slice them lengthwise into thick strips.
Salt the eggplant slices and let them sit for 20 minutes to draw out bitterness, then pat dry.
Heat oil in a large pan and fry the eggplant slices in batches until golden brown on both sides, then set aside.
In the same pan, sauté one sliced onion until deep golden and crispy, then remove and reserve for garnish.
Sauté the second chopped onion with the minced garlic and turmeric until soft.
Mash the fried eggplant and mix it into the pan with the sautéed onion and garlic.
Stir in the kashk, salt, and black pepper, cooking gently for 5 minutes until well combined.
Transfer to a serving dish and top with the crispy onions.
In a small pan, heat a little oil with dried mint until fragrant, then drizzle over the top before serving.

title: Aash-e Reshteh
instructions: Soak the chickpeas and kidney beans overnight, then boil them in the water until tender.
Add the lentils to the pot and cook for another 20 minutes.
Finely chop the spinach, parsley, cilantro, and chives.
Sauté one chopped onion in oil until golden, then add the chopped herbs and cook down for 15 minutes.
Add the sautéed herbs to the pot of beans and simmer for 20 minutes.
Break the reshteh noodles into shorter pieces and add them to the pot, cooking until tender.
Season with salt and black pepper, adjusting the consistency with extra water if the soup is too thick.
Fry the remaining sliced onion and minced garlic in oil until golden and crispy, then stir the garlic and half the kashk into the soup.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the remaining kashk, fried onions, and a drizzle of oil infused with dried mint.

title: Baghali Polo
instructions: Rinse the basmati rice thoroughly and soak in salted water for 1 hour.
Bloom the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and parboil the drained rice for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain.
Chop the fresh dill and set aside.
Layer a third of the parboiled rice in a pot, then sprinkle with a layer of fava beans and dill.
Repeat layering the rice, fava beans, and dill until all ingredients are used, finishing with a rice layer.
Drizzle melted butter over the top and cover the pot with a towel-wrapped lid.
Steam on low heat for 40 to 45 minutes until the rice is fully cooked and fluffy.
Spoon out a portion of rice and mix with the bloomed saffron water before serving as garnish on top.

title: Khoresh Bademjan
instructions: Peel the eggplants, slice lengthwise, salt them, and let sit for 20 minutes to remove bitterness, then pat dry.
Fry the eggplant slices in oil until golden on both sides, then set aside on paper towels.
In a pot, heat oil and sauté the diced onion until golden.
Add the beef and turmeric, browning the meat on all sides.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, then add the water.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes until the meat is tender.
Slice the tomatoes and layer them with the fried eggplant on top of the stew.
Add the lemon juice, salt, and black pepper, then cover and simmer gently for another 20 minutes without stirring to keep the eggplant intact.
Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Shirazi Salad
instructions: Dice the cucumbers, tomatoes, and onion into small, uniform cubes.
Combine the diced vegetables in a large mixing bowl.
Add the lime juice, olive oil, and dried mint to the bowl.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Toss everything together well until evenly coated.
Chill the salad in the refrigerator for at least 10 minutes before serving.

title: Torshi Liteh
instructions: Roast the whole eggplants over an open flame or under a broiler until the skin is charred and the flesh is soft.
Let the eggplants cool, then peel off the skin and mash the flesh in a bowl.
Finely chop the mixed vegetables and mince the garlic.
Combine the mashed eggplant with the chopped vegetables and minced garlic.
Stir in the dried mint, salt, and black pepper.
Pour in the white vinegar and mix thoroughly until well combined.
Transfer the mixture into a clean sterilized jar.
Seal the jar and refrigerate for at least 3 days before serving to let the flavors develop.

title: Sholeh Zard
instructions: Rinse the rice thoroughly and soak in water for 1 hour, then drain.
Bring the water to a boil in a large pot and add the drained rice.
Simmer the rice over low heat, stirring occasionally, for 45 minutes until it breaks down and thickens.
Bloom the saffron in a small amount of hot water and add it to the pot.
Stir in the sugar and continue simmering for 20 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking.
Add the rose water and oil, stirring well to combine.
Cook for another 10 minutes until the pudding reaches a smooth, thick consistency.
Pour into serving bowls and smooth the tops.
Garnish with slivered almonds and a sprinkle of cinnamon before serving warm or chilled.

title: Faloodeh
instructions: Boil the water with sugar in a saucepan until the sugar fully dissolves to form a syrup.
Remove from heat and stir in the rose water, then let the syrup cool completely.
Cook the thin vermicelli noodles in boiling water for 1 to 2 minutes until just tender, then drain and rinse with cold water.
Combine the cooled noodles with the rose water syrup in a bowl.
Pour the mixture into a shallow container and freeze for about 3 to 4 hours, stirring every hour to break up ice crystals.
Once the mixture reaches a slushy, semi-frozen texture, scoop it into serving glasses.
Drizzle each serving with fresh lime juice just before serving.

title: Barbari Bread
instructions: In a large bowl, combine the bread flour, instant yeast, sugar, and salt.
Add the vegetable oil and warm water, then mix and knead into a soft, smooth dough for about 10 minutes.
Cover the dough and let it rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled in size.
Meanwhile, make the roomal glaze by whisking the tablespoon of flour with the 3 tablespoons of water over low heat until it thickens slightly, then let it cool.
Divide the dough into two portions and shape each into a long, flat oval on a baking sheet.
Use your fingers to press deep grooves lengthwise into the dough.
Brush the roomal glaze over the surface and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Let the shaped loaves rest for 20 minutes while preheating the oven to 230°C (450°F).
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until the crust is golden brown and crisp.
Cool slightly on a rack before slicing and serving.

title: Ash-e Doogh
instructions: Rinse the rice and cook it in the water over medium heat for 15 minutes until softened.
Whisk the chickpea flour into the yogurt drink until smooth, then slowly add it to the pot, stirring constantly to prevent curdling.
Finely chop the spinach and cilantro and add them to the pot.
Simmer over low heat for 30 minutes, stirring frequently.
Beat the eggs and slowly stream them into the simmering soup while stirring gently to form thin ribbons.
Season with salt and black pepper.
In a separate pan, sauté the sliced onions in oil until golden and crispy.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the crispy fried onions.
Finish with a drizzle of oil infused with dried mint before serving.

title: Dizi
instructions: Soak the chickpeas and white beans overnight, then drain.
In a large pot, combine the lamb shank, soaked beans, chopped onions, turmeric, salt, and black pepper.
Add the water and bring to a boil, skimming off any foam that rises.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 1.5 hours.
Add the whole peeled potatoes, chopped tomatoes, and tomato paste to the pot.
Continue simmering for another 45 minutes until the meat is fall-apart tender and potatoes are cooked through.
Carefully strain the broth into a separate bowl, reserving the solids.
Mash the solid ingredients together in a separate dish until well combined.
Serve the broth as a first course with bread, followed by the mashed meat and vegetable mixture.

title: Kuku Sabzi
instructions: Finely chop the parsley, cilantro, dill, and chives.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs until well beaten.
Add the chopped herbs, flour, baking powder, salt, and black pepper to the eggs and mix thoroughly.
Rinse the barberries and fold half of them into the batter.
Heat the oil in a nonstick pan over medium heat.
Pour the batter into the pan, spreading it evenly, and sprinkle the remaining barberries on top.
Cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes until the bottom is golden and the top is mostly set.
Carefully flip the kuku using a plate and cook the other side for another 10 minutes until golden brown.
Slice into wedges and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Ash-e Anar
instructions: Rinse the rice and yellow split peas, then cook them together in the water over medium heat for 30 minutes until soft.
Finely chop the spinach, parsley, and mint leaves.
Sauté one chopped onion in oil until golden, then add the chopped herbs and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the sautéed herbs to the pot of rice and split peas.
Pour in the pomegranate juice and sugar, then simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Season with salt and black pepper, adjusting sweetness or tartness with more sugar or pomegranate juice as needed.
Fry the remaining sliced onion in oil until crispy and golden.
Ladle the soup into bowls and top with the crispy fried onions before serving.

title: Mirza Ghasemi
instructions: Roast the whole eggplants over an open flame or under a broiler until the skin is charred and the flesh is tender.
Let the eggplants cool, peel off the skin, and roughly mash the flesh.
Heat oil in a large pan and sauté the minced garlic until fragrant.
Grate or finely chop the tomatoes and add them to the pan along with turmeric.
Cook the tomatoes down for 10 minutes until they break apart and thicken.
Add the mashed eggplant to the pan and stir well to combine with the tomato mixture.
Season with salt and black pepper, and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Beat the eggs and pour them into the pan, stirring constantly until they are just cooked through.
Serve hot with fresh bread.

title: Adas Polo
instructions: Rinse the basmati rice and soak in salted water for 1 hour, then drain.
Rinse the lentils and cook them in a separate pot of water for 15 minutes until just tender but not mushy, then drain.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and parboil the rice for 6 to 8 minutes, then drain.
Thinly slice one onion and fry in oil until deep golden and crispy, then set aside.
Sauté the remaining chopped onion in oil until soft, then stir in the raisins and cinnamon for 2 minutes.
Combine the cooked lentils with the sautéed onion and raisin mixture.
Layer the parboiled rice and lentil mixture alternately in a pot, finishing with a rice layer.
Drizzle with a little oil, cover with a towel-wrapped lid, and steam on low heat for 40 minutes.
Gently mix before serving and top with the crispy fried onions.

title: Khoresh Gheimeh
instructions: Heat oil in a pot and sauté the diced onion until golden.
Add the beef and turmeric, browning the meat on all sides.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the water and prick the dried limes with a fork before adding them to the pot.
Season with salt and black pepper, then cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Rinse the split peas and add them to the pot, simmering for another 30 minutes until the peas and meat are tender.
Meanwhile, cut the potatoes into thin strips and deep fry them until golden and crisp.
Once the stew has thickened, adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot over steamed rice, topped with the crispy fried potato strips.

title: Ranginak
instructions: Pit the dates and stuff each one with a piece of walnut, then arrange them in a single layer in a baking dish.
Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat.
Add the flour and turmeric to the melted butter, stirring constantly to avoid burning.
Toast the flour mixture for 8 to 10 minutes until it turns golden brown and fragrant.
Stir in the cinnamon and remove the pan from heat.
Spread the toasted flour mixture evenly over the stuffed dates, covering them completely.
Let the dish cool to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour to firm up.
Garnish with slivered pistachios before slicing into squares and serving.

title: Doogh
instructions: Whisk the yogurt in a large pitcher until smooth.
Gradually add the water while whisking continuously until fully combined.
Stir in the salt and dried mint.
Taste and adjust the salt or dilution level as preferred.
Pour into glasses filled with ice cubes and serve immediately.

title: Halim
instructions: Soak the wheat berries in water overnight, then drain.
Combine the soaked wheat berries with fresh water in a large pot and bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer for 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the wheat is very soft and starting to break down.
Add the shredded chicken to the pot and continue cooking for 30 minutes.
Using a whisk or immersion blender, beat the mixture vigorously until it becomes a smooth, thick paste.
Season with salt and stir in half of the butter.
Continue cooking on low heat for another 20 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent sticking.
Spoon the halim into serving bowls and top with the remaining melted butter.
Sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon before serving hot.

title: Nane Berenji
instructions: Bloom the saffron in 2 tablespoons of hot water.
In a large bowl, whisk together the sugar and vegetable oil until well combined.
Add the egg yolks and bloomed saffron water, whisking until smooth.
Gradually fold in the rice flour until a soft, pliable dough forms.
Cover the dough and let it rest at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 160°C (320°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Pipe or shape small rounds of dough onto the baking sheet, spacing them apart.
Sprinkle each cookie with a few poppy seeds.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until the bottoms are just set but the cookies remain pale.
Let the cookies cool completely on the tray before removing, as they are delicate while warm.
